## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicBeta.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicBeta.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) and the model probability ratio, which is: P(new) / P(old) This implementation produces a sample using generateRandomness, which means that: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) = P(old) / P(new) We use the fact that this element can compute densities for values to compute P(new) and P(old) explicitly. Note that the two returned ratios will still multiply to 1. This does not affect normal Metropolis-Hastings, but helps the Metropolis-Hastings annealer find maxima. Attributes Definition Classes HasDensity -> Element Inherited from: HasDensity

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.nextRandomness(oldRandomness)
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicDirichlet.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicDirichlet.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicDirichlet.nextRandomness ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicDirichlet.html#nextRandomness-fffff446)

```scala
override def nextRandomness(oldRandomness: Randomness): (Randomness, Double, Double)
```

Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is:

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` oldRandomness: Randomness ``.

Returns: `` (Randomness, Double, Double) ``.

Source contract/attributes: Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) and the model probability ratio, which is: P(new) / P(old) This implementation produces a sample using generateRandomness, which means that: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) = P(old) / P(new) We use the fact that this element can compute densities for values to compute P(new) and P(old) explicitly. Note that the two returned ratios will still multiply to 1. This does not affect normal Metropolis-Hastings, but helps the Metropolis-Hastings annealer find maxima. Attributes Definition Classes HasDensity -> Element Inherited from: HasDensity

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.nextRandomness(oldRandomness)
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicExponential.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicExponential.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicExponential.nextRandomness ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicExponential.html#nextRandomness-fffff446)

```scala
override def nextRandomness(oldRandomness: Randomness): (Randomness, Double, Double)
```

Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is:

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` oldRandomness: Randomness ``.

Returns: `` (Randomness, Double, Double) ``.

Source contract/attributes: Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) and the model probability ratio, which is: P(new) / P(old) This implementation produces a sample using generateRandomness, which means that: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) = P(old) / P(new) We use the fact that this element can compute densities for values to compute P(new) and P(old) explicitly. Note that the two returned ratios will still multiply to 1. This does not affect normal Metropolis-Hastings, but helps the Metropolis-Hastings annealer find maxima. Attributes Definition Classes HasDensity -> Element Inherited from: HasDensity

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.nextRandomness(oldRandomness)
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicGamma.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicGamma.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicGamma.nextRandomness ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicGamma.html#nextRandomness-fffff446)

```scala
override def nextRandomness(oldRandomness: Randomness): (Randomness, Double, Double)
```

Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is:

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` oldRandomness: Randomness ``.

Returns: `` (Randomness, Double, Double) ``.

Source contract/attributes: Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) and the model probability ratio, which is: P(new) / P(old) This implementation produces a sample using generateRandomness, which means that: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) = P(old) / P(new) We use the fact that this element can compute densities for values to compute P(new) and P(old) explicitly. Note that the two returned ratios will still multiply to 1. This does not affect normal Metropolis-Hastings, but helps the Metropolis-Hastings annealer find maxima. Attributes Definition Classes HasDensity -> Element Inherited from: HasDensity

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.nextRandomness(oldRandomness)
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicInverseGamma.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicInverseGamma.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicInverseGamma.nextRandomness ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicInverseGamma.html#nextRandomness-fffff446)

```scala
override def nextRandomness(oldRandomness: Randomness): (Randomness, Double, Double)
```

Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is:

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` oldRandomness: Randomness ``.

Returns: `` (Randomness, Double, Double) ``.

Source contract/attributes: Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) and the model probability ratio, which is: P(new) / P(old) This implementation produces a sample using generateRandomness, which means that: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) = P(old) / P(new) We use the fact that this element can compute densities for values to compute P(new) and P(old) explicitly. Note that the two returned ratios will still multiply to 1. This does not affect normal Metropolis-Hastings, but helps the Metropolis-Hastings annealer find maxima. Attributes Definition Classes HasDensity -> Element Inherited from: HasDensity

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.nextRandomness(oldRandomness)
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicMultivariateNormal.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicMultivariateNormal.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicMultivariateNormal.nextRandomness ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicMultivariateNormal.html#nextRandomness-fffff446)

```scala
override def nextRandomness(oldRandomness: Randomness): (Randomness, Double, Double)
```

Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is:

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` oldRandomness: Randomness ``.

Returns: `` (Randomness, Double, Double) ``.

Source contract/attributes: Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) and the model probability ratio, which is: P(new) / P(old) This implementation produces a sample using generateRandomness, which means that: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) = P(old) / P(new) We use the fact that this element can compute densities for values to compute P(new) and P(old) explicitly. Note that the two returned ratios will still multiply to 1. This does not affect normal Metropolis-Hastings, but helps the Metropolis-Hastings annealer find maxima. Attributes Definition Classes HasDensity -> Element Inherited from: HasDensity

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.nextRandomness(oldRandomness)
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicNormal.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicNormal.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicNormal.nextRandomness ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicNormal.html#nextRandomness-fffff446)

```scala
override def nextRandomness(oldRandomness: Randomness): (Randomness, Double, Double)
```

Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is:

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` oldRandomness: Randomness ``.

Returns: `` (Randomness, Double, Double) ``.

Source contract/attributes: Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) and the model probability ratio, which is: P(new) / P(old) This implementation produces a sample using generateRandomness, which means that: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) = P(old) / P(new) We use the fact that this element can compute densities for values to compute P(new) and P(old) explicitly. Note that the two returned ratios will still multiply to 1. This does not affect normal Metropolis-Hastings, but helps the Metropolis-Hastings annealer find maxima. Attributes Definition Classes HasDensity -> Element Inherited from: HasDensity

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.nextRandomness(oldRandomness)
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicUniform.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicUniform.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.AtomicUniform.nextRandomness ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/AtomicUniform.html#nextRandomness-fffff446)

```scala
override def nextRandomness(oldRandomness: Randomness): (Randomness, Double, Double)
```

Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is:

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` oldRandomness: Randomness ``.

Returns: `` (Randomness, Double, Double) ``.

Source contract/attributes: Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) and the model probability ratio, which is: P(new) / P(old) This implementation produces a sample using generateRandomness, which means that: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) = P(old) / P(new) We use the fact that this element can compute densities for values to compute P(new) and P(old) explicitly. Note that the two returned ratios will still multiply to 1. This does not affect normal Metropolis-Hastings, but helps the Metropolis-Hastings annealer find maxima. Attributes Definition Classes HasDensity -> Element Inherited from: HasDensity

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.nextRandomness(oldRandomness)
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.Beta.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/Beta.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.CompoundBeta.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/CompoundBeta.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.CompoundDirichlet.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/CompoundDirichlet.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.CompoundExponential.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/CompoundExponential.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.CompoundGamma.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/CompoundGamma.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.CompoundNormal.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/CompoundNormal.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.CompoundUniform.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/CompoundUniform.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.Dirichlet.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/Dirichlet.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.Exponential.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/Exponential.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.Gamma.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/Gamma.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.GammaCompoundK.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/GammaCompoundK.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.InverseGamma.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/InverseGamma.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.KernelDensity.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/KernelDensity.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.KernelDensity.nextRandomness ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/KernelDensity.html#nextRandomness-fffff446)

```scala
override def nextRandomness(oldRandomness: Randomness): (Randomness, Double, Double)
```

Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is:

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` oldRandomness: Randomness ``.

Returns: `` (Randomness, Double, Double) ``.

Source contract/attributes: Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) and the model probability ratio, which is: P(new) / P(old) This implementation produces a sample using generateRandomness, which means that: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) = P(old) / P(new) We use the fact that this element can compute densities for values to compute P(new) and P(old) explicitly. Note that the two returned ratios will still multiply to 1. This does not affect normal Metropolis-Hastings, but helps the Metropolis-Hastings annealer find maxima. Attributes Definition Classes HasDensity -> Element Inherited from: HasDensity

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.nextRandomness(oldRandomness)
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.MultivariateCompoundNormal.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/MultivariateCompoundNormal.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.MultivariateNormal.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/MultivariateNormal.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.MultivariateNormalCompoundMean.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/MultivariateNormalCompoundMean.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.Normal.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/Normal.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.NormalCompoundMean.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/NormalCompoundMean.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.NormalCompoundVariance.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/NormalCompoundVariance.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.library.atomic.continuous.Uniform.elementsIAmContingentOn ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/library/atomic/continuous/Uniform.html#elementsIAmContingentOn-0)

```scala
def elementsIAmContingentOn: Set[Element[_]]
```

Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters: none (parameterless member; do not append `()`).

Returns: `` Set[Element[_]] ``.

Source contract/attributes: Returns the elements that this element is contingent on. These are elements that are required to have a certain value for a condition or constraint to be relevant to this element. The contingency is required because conditions and constraints can be applied to references that are uncertain. Every possible element that could be pointed to by a reference must be given the condition or constraint, but the condition or constraint only applies if the elements earlier in the reference have the required value. Figaro takes care of handling all this under the hood. However, some algorithms may need to know which elements an element is contingent on. For example, sampling algorithms may need to sample those other elements first. This method is supplied to support this use case. Attributes Inherited from: Element

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.elementsIAmContingentOn
```

Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is:

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` rand: Randomness ``.

Returns: `` (Randomness, Double, Double) ``.

Source contract/attributes: Generate the next randomness given the current randomness. Returns three values: The next randomness, the Metropolis-Hastings proposal probability ratio, which is: P(new -> old) / P(old -> new) and the model probability ratio, which is: P(new) / P(old) The default implementation is to use generateRandomness and returns ones for the proposal and model probability ratios. Attributes Inherited from: Element
